sections.title: Reference-inset inpaint copies the character but not the style? Strip the quality tags and zero the UC
sections.lede: omni could get advanced reference inpainting to copy a character but not its style. mahouko's fix was one line: take every quality tag out and set the UC to None with an empty string.
sections.body:
Advanced reference inpainting (the docs call it that, and omni was careful to say it is not the PR tool) works by pasting a reference on the canvas and inpainting the rest. omni reported that identity carried well but the drawing style did not, unless they inpainted inside the reference itself, and guessed a tag was missing.

mahouko's answer wasn't a missing tag. It was the stuff on top: **get rid of every quality tag in your prompt, and set your UC to None and an empty string.** The quality preset and UC presets push the image toward a house look, and that pull fights the reference's style. omni's reply ('muh complexity') points at the one thing they rely on: the complexity tag. Test with and without it, because mahouko said every quality tag.

This sits next to the guide's existing PR substitutes (reference sheet tags, reference inset, inpaint the rest). It doesn't replace them.

**Try this.** Paste a small reference in a corner of a blank canvas and mask everything else.
A (control): your usual prompt with Quality Tags on and the Light UC preset.
B: same prompt with Quality Tags **off**, UC preset **None**, UC field empty.
C: B plus `high complexity` only.
Prompt starter: `1girl, solo, cowboy shot, standing, simple background, reference inset, image includes character reference`
Settings: V5 Full · inpaint · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · same seed and mask for A/B/C.

**CTA.** If B matches the reference's line and colour better than A, `save_memory` it under a ref-inset name. If C undoes the gain, complexity counts as a quality tag for this job.

excerpts.speaker: omni
excerpts.text: I can get reference inset inpainting to copy a character well but style replication still is tricky, I figure I am missing a tag and it not like the model can't do it but I have to basically inpaint within the pic itself, anyone else been fiddling with reference inpainting?

excerpts.speaker: mahouko (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: get rid of every quality tag in your prompt, and set your UC to None and empty string

excerpts.speaker: omni
excerpts.text: muh complexity but yea that the only thing I have, UC always be pretty slim to none

sections.title: Price one image while it's free, and read your V5 battery from the API
sections.lede: No public formula for the meter, but ght901 gave a trick that works in the UI, and arda named the API field.
sections.body:
Silver asked for the formula behind the Anlas cost, hoping to predict how much V5 usage a setting burns. ght901: it's not secret, the calculation runs in your browser, but there are **too many edge cases and exceptions for different models and features to give a simple formula**. The trick: when a gen shows 0 Anlas, **set the image count to 2**. The first image is free, so the price you see is the price of one image.

For tool builders (Menma, Frost), Cheshire asked whether the V5 Opus budget is visible over the API. After one 'sorry, misinformation' and a correction, arda named it: **`GET https://image.novelai.net/user/data`, under `.subscription.usage`.** It's in `nai-staff-updates/digest.md` for the proxy folks.

Community footnotes: the bar doesn't fill past 100%, so leaving it full overnight wastes refills (Flitter, Uragan). Whooters asked whether a '14% refresh rate' gives about 242 images a day at 22 steps with no net loss. Nobody on staff confirmed the math, so treat it as a user estimate.

**Try this.** Turn on any feature you're unsure about (larger resolution, more steps, Enhance), set image count to 2, and write down the number shown. That's your per-image Anlas price for that setup, the same number the browser uses to price it.

**CTA.** Menma: if Dreamscape shows a battery gauge, try reading `.subscription.usage` from `/user/data` instead of estimating. Board it through Rook if it's worth a ticket.

excerpts.speaker: ght901 (Anlatan)
excerpts.text:
When the cost is zero you can just set it to generate two images to see the price of one. Since the first one is costs zero, the price you see is the price of a single image.
It's not really a secret. The calculation is happening inside your browser. There's just too many edge cases and exceptions for different models and features to give a simple formula

excerpts.speaker: arda (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: actually it wasnt misinformation, my bad

excerpts.speaker: arda (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: check `GET https://image.novelai.net/user/data` , it should be under .subscription.usage of the JSON

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text: You are wasting usage by leaving it at 100%, but I don't think there's a need to use it more if your average use is inferior to the refill rate.

sections.title: "The style wears off": it doesn't, and a nonsense line proves how easily a seed moves
sections.lede: MommysAI felt their style fade over a session of random-seed gens. OccultSage: same seed plus same prompt doesn't change. What wears out is the viewer.
sections.body:
The question comes up every few weeks: 'is anyone else getting inconsistencies?' OccultSage asked the only useful first question: **same seed, same prompt?** If yes, share both images with metadata. MommysAI was on random seeds, and the answer was deadpan: '... it doesn't wear off. What wears out is your eyeball and perceptions.' The thread got heated and ended with an apology and a friendly reply. The technical point stands, and it matches the guide's STAFF notes (seed quality isn't time-of-day; maintenance or GPU changes can break bit-identical repro, but the model doesn't fade).

Bicknell125 added the practical part. Some seeds fight your whole prompt. To tell an unlucky seed from an unstable style, **freeze the seed and remove your artstyle chunk**, then look at what's left. A day earlier Bicknell posted a pair on one seed, the second with a **meaningless pop-song line** added. The images differ visibly. Any prose changes the image somewhat, so check a 'discovery' on several seeds before you call it a magic prompt.

Related (ShaddAI / Bicknell125): hair colours come out lighter in some styles. Colour tags don't map the same across artstyles, so tune the hair tag per style.

**Try this.** Three seeds × two arms. A = your prompt. B = your prompt plus one irrelevant sentence (`the radio is playing an old song.`). If B 'improves' one seed and not the others, it's noise.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light.

**CTA.** Before you write a technique up, run it on three seeds minimum. That's already the Cellar's lab standard. This is why.

excerpts.speaker: OccultSage (Anlatan)
excerpts.text:
Do you have the same seed, the same prompt?

If so, share both images that show the inconsistency with metadata embedded.

excerpts.speaker: OccultSage (Anlatan)
excerpts.text:
... it doesn't wear off.

What wears out is your eyeball and perceptions.

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: Sometimes you get a seed that just is working against all your prompts. The easiest way to tell that is to freeze it and check what's being generated when your artstyle chunk is removed

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: These two images were made in the same seed but the latter one I added a nonsense pop song line to it. If you're not careful you'll mistake these sorts of things for magic prompts, when it was just random changes due to you putting a prose tag with no particular meaning

sections.title: Nudge style from the UC, and call the halftone dots by their real name
sections.lede: CCYKM found that a weak positive style tag can do nothing at all on some seeds, while a negative weight in the UC always does a little. Uragan named the dot pattern people keep fighting.
sections.body:
CCYKM's trick: instead of `0.5::flat color::`, `0.5::jaggy lines::` or `0.5::ligne claire::` in the prompt to lean a style, put **`-2::flat color::` in the UC**. Low positive weights 'sometimes just straight up don't do anything depending on the seed', but the UC negative 'always has an effect, but a slight one'. In NAI terms a negative weight in the UC un-suppresses, so it acts as a gentle positive pull. stoppedloss added the other direction: `2::flat color::` in the prompt gives 'nicely saturated images'.

appopolo wanted solid colours instead of a dot texture. Nemuidere suggested a negative weight on `halftone`. Uragan gave the actual tag: **`ben-day dots`**, so `-1::ben-day dots::`. Uragan also said: if you've written your own UC, **turn the Heavy UC preset off**, because 'preset heavy UC is just bad' when stacked on a custom UC. The guide already says that (custom UC means preset off).

From the multi-artist thread (Varg / Uragan): extra floating heads with several artist tags happen because multi-artist Danbooru posts are usually collabs where each artist drew their own character. `-6::artist collaboration::` (Uragan says -8 or -10 has no side effects) or just `solo` fixes it. The guide keeps the V5 caveat that this is case by case.

**Try this.** Same seed, three arms:
A prompt `0.5::flat color::` · B UC `-2::flat color::` · C neither.
Prompt: `1girl, solo, upper body, short black hair, glasses, white hoodie, pink background, high complexity`
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light (B adds the line).
Halftone check: add `screentone, halftone` to the prompt for a dotty base, then `-1::ben-day dots::` on the same seed.

**CTA.** Guren: does B move the style on every seed while A sometimes doesn't move it? Three seeds is enough to call it.

excerpts.speaker: CCYKM
excerpts.text: Instead of using stuff like 0.5::flat color:: or 0.5::jaggy lines:: or 0.5::ligne claire:: or whatnot to nudge the artstyle in a certain direction, it's better to put them in UC as -2::flat color:: and stuff like that

excerpts.speaker: CCYKM
excerpts.text: because if you try to use tags at too low power sometimes they just straight up don't do anything depending on the seed

excerpts.speaker: stoppedloss
excerpts.text: inversely if you do 2::flat color:: you get nicely saturated images

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text:
Actual tag for this is `ben-day dots`, so just put `-1::ben-day dots::` and good to go.
Also, unrelated, but you should remove the preset UC, you already have a UC, and preset heavy UC is just bad

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text:
It's actually not that it interprets the artist tags as other characters, but because having multiple artists on danbooru 99% of the time means artists made their own characters on the same picture. But if you have just one character, it can't make those. So instead, it makes up faces out of nowhere.
Solution for that is `-6::artist collaboration::`. You can increase it to -8 or -10, it doesn't have side effects at those strengths.

sections.title: Make them actually hug: tags that close the gap, and how to get both hands held
sections.lede: Strawberry Mk.VI's cuddling pair kept sleeping a foot apart. Two regulars fixed it from different angles, and a hand-holding thread found its culprit in the collarbones.
sections.body:
The prompt was a careful one: Deltarune's Kris and Susie under the covers, `source#cicada hug` / `target#cicada hug`, `mutual#belly-to-belly`, NL 'she tightly cuddles kris'. They still came out apart.

Kirari~n's diagnosis had three parts. First, **don't tag details you couldn't see if they were pressed together** (the front of her pajamas, say). The model makes room to show them. Second, `cicada hug` has about a hundred Danbooru posts and a name that doesn't describe itself. Write `hugging with arms and legs`. Third, prefer direct visual description: `holding him close to her body` beats `tightly cuddles`.

Bicknell125 posted a tag set that reliably closes the gap: **`mutual hug, clinging, belly-to-belly, arms around neck, arms around another's waist, hands on another's back, cheek press, breast compress`**.

Then 'I am Rocket Science' couldn't get two girls holding **both** hands. Bicknell: `holding hands` has tens of thousands of examples of *one* hand, so it pulls the wrong way. Try `double hand grab`. Redwood Elf uses `fingers interlaced`. When it still failed, Bicknell gave the standard method: wipe the prompt, get the hands working alone on a fixed seed, add your tags back until it breaks. It was **the collarbone tags**.

**Try this.** Two character boxes (girl, girl), base `2girls, cowboy shot, indoors, bedroom, night`.
Box 1: `girl, long red hair, grey sweater, mutual hug, clinging, belly-to-belly, arms around neck, cheek press, smile, closed eyes`
Box 2: `girl, short brown hair, white shirt, mutual hug, arms around another's waist, hands on another's back, cheek press, blush`
Both-hands variant: swap the hug tags for `facing another, double hand grab, fingers interlaced, looking at another`.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23–28 (two characters) · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light.

**CTA.** If the hug holds on 3 seeds, `save_memory` the tag set. If one tag adds a gap back, note which one.

excerpts.speaker: Strawberry Mk.VI
excerpts.text:
What tagging gives characters that *actually* hug closely?
I have this on both characters:
`sleeping, source#cicada hug, under covers, lying on side, source#cuddling, expressionless. She tightly cuddles him. mutual#belly-to-belly, `
but they're always some distance apart.

excerpts.speaker: Kirari~n ☆
excerpts.text:
are those the the only tags? one thing that often sabotages such prompts is if you tag details that would not be easily discernable if their bodies are close. like if you describe, uh...the front of the girl's pajamas.
also, `cicada hug` probably isn't a very good tag to use. it has like 100 posts on danbooru, and it's not obvious what it means from the words alone. I'd prefer using something like `hugging with arms and legs`.
and while `tightly cuddles` is a valid description, you might have more luck with a more direct visual description, like `holding him close to her body`.

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text:
These are the tags I use for hugs to make them tighter:
mutual hug, clinging, belly-to-belly, arms around neck, arms around another's waist, hands on another's back, cheek press, breast compress,

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: holding hands is going to have tens of thousands of datapoints of one hand each

excerpts.speaker: I am Rocket Science
excerpts.text: It's the collarbone prompts

sections.title: An empty room with no one in it, and a background you can reuse without PR
sections.lede: Fermuto had a full UC of people tags and still got an anime girl in every background. The fix was mostly in the boxes.
sections.body:
Fermuto tried `no human, scenery` and a UC listing 'people, boy, girl'. The answers: the tag is **`no humans`** (plural, Nemuidere), and **make sure no character prompts are on**, because an enabled box asks for a person even when the base prompt says otherwise. Another user suggested moving the people words into the main prompt with a negative weight, and that got a clean result 'at least once'. deleted_user noted that even with Quality Tags on they could keep characters out.

The older, harder case is continuity. Magical Nate wanted the same background across images, but Precise Reference flips the model back to V4.5. Redwood Elf's workflow: **render the background alone, render the characters on a blank background, composite in Krita.** Even `-10::girl,boy,student,character:: 10::background only::` doesn't always keep people out, so expect a few rerolls. The composite loses valid NAI metadata. Redwood used Krita's magic wand to clear hair gaps for the cut-out.

Related (c0dey_, Degeneracy): for different artists on the background and the characters, inpaint one region at a time with **Focused Inpainting**, using only that part of the prompt plus its artist tags. Selecting just the background by hand is the painful part.

**Try this.** Base: `no humans, scenery, indoors, long stone corridor, arched windows, sunlight, tiled floor, high complexity`. Every character box **off**. UC Light.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on.
If a figure still appears, try the base-prompt negative `-2::1girl, 1boy, person::` before adding more UC.

**CTA.** Ivory: this suits Studio. A background-only preset with boxes forced off would save people this whole thread.

excerpts.speaker: Fermuto
excerpts.text: No matter what I put the model insists on inserting an anime girl

excerpts.speaker: Mysterious One - Nemuidere
excerpts.text: Make sure no character prompts are on. That can cause unexpected behavior when they should be off.

excerpts.speaker: Redwood Elf
excerpts.text: If you really want the same background, render a background by itself with no characters, then use Krita (or some other image editing software) to add the characters in separately by having NAI render the characters with a blank background.

excerpts.speaker: c0dey_
excerpts.text: Take a part of your prompt and only use that to inpaint one of the characters at a time with focused inpainting (to reduce bleed). Focused inpainting is very good at this, since only a part of the image is passed to the model before being resized

images.cap: Background rendered alone, ready to composite

sections.title: Still no V5 Precise Reference: img2img at about 0.57 is the stopgap people are using
sections.lede: 'pr soon?' was the most common message of the window. Meanwhile one user found V5 img2img carrying an outfit from a source image well enough to call it a rough PR.
sections.body:
He makes zombies posted a source and a V5 img2img result: 'Holy crap it really can be used as a pseudo PR.' **Around 0.57 strength**, img2img took 'a lot of the weight off of text prompting for things like clothes or things that don't have tags'. The guide already warns that V5 img2img overwrites more at low strength than V4.5 did (staff), so 0.57 is a starting point to tune, not a constant.

Sigurd cleared up inpainting: **V5 Full uses the V5 Full inpainting model; V5 Curated uses the V4.5 Curated one**, because there's no V5 Curated inpaint model yet. That's already in the guide. If Curated inpaint looks bad, that's why.

On the rumour mill: someone in the official channel said 'PR teasers start tomorrow'. That's a community claim, not staff. Uchariko's 'When it's ready™' is the honest status.

**Try this.** Gen or pick a character in an outfit you can't tag. Use it as the img2img source with a prompt that names the pose and setting, not the clothes: `1girl, solo, full body, standing, hand on hip, city street, daytime, high complexity`.
Strength ladder: 0.45 / 0.57 / 0.70, same seed.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light.

**CTA.** Find where the outfit survives and the pose changes. Note the strength and `save_memory` it as a V5 PR stopgap.

excerpts.speaker: He makes zombies
excerpts.text: Yeah i2i at around .57 strength can be used as a rudimentary PR and take a lot of the weight off of text prompting for things like clothes or things that don't have tags

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum} 🔋
excerpts.text: inpainting on V5 Full uses the V5 Full inpainting model. inpainting on V5 Curated uses the V4.5 Curated inpainting model (since there's no V5 Curated inpainting model yet)

sections.title: artist: beats a bare name, label words aren't free on V5, and res_mult is real but mild
sections.lede: Three small things that save rerolls.
sections.body:
**artist: prefix.** Blk01 asked whether a bare Danbooru name works. Triplis: `artist:name` is the strongest, most reliable form. A bare `name` can work but is weaker, and 'sometimes even `artist:partial artist name` will do something', with `1girl, artist:glossyspicy, portrait` as an example of a half-real tag doing something anyway. The guide already says to prefix artists.

**Label words move V5 style.** On V4.5 shambibble put `megan` near the front of every Megan prompt so filenames were searchable, and it barely mattered. On V5 it 'had strong effects on the style even with a full chunk'. Sigurd's fix keeps labels out of the prompt: in **debug settings, set a custom filename template with `{characters}`**, then name your character boxes (click the `Character 1` label to type a name). The name goes into the filename and doesn't change the image.

**res_mult.** NalathniDragon asked for the 'treat this as higher resolution' tag. `absurd res` was a guess. Uchariko pointed to **`res_mult:#x`**, and Flitter said it was trained in and the effect is 'mild but real'. Don't expect it to stand in for actually upscaling.

**Try this.** `1girl, solo, portrait, artist:glossyspicy` vs `1girl, solo, portrait, glossyspicy` on one seed. Then `res_mult:2x` vs nothing on one seed.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light.

**CTA.** If you name files with prompt words today, switch to `{characters}` and compare one old seed.

excerpts.speaker: Triplis
excerpts.text: `artist:name` is the strongest/most reliable way to prompt it. `name` may work too but is weaker/less reliable

excerpts.speaker: shambibble
excerpts.text: in 4.5 i put "megan" near the front of all of my megan prompts so i they would be in the filename and i could easily search them up, because they had so many tags on the back end it rarely affected anything. in v5 i rapidly discovered this had strong effects on the style even with a full chunk

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum} 🔋
excerpts.text: In debug settings you can set a custom file name template, one of the features being `{characters}` for named character prompt boxes (you can click on the `Character 1` display to type in a name), which afaik would be the only way to automatically save varying input text to the filename without having any impact on the output.

excerpts.speaker: {Flitter}
excerpts.text: It was trained in, and the effect is mild but real

sections.title: Weekend lab board: six cheap A/Bs, free gens only
sections.lede: For Guren and anyone with a full battery. Small portraits, Opus-free, three seeds each.
sections.body:
1. **Ref-inset style match.** Quality on + Light UC vs Quality off + UC None + empty, then + `high complexity` (staff article).
2. **UC style nudge.** `0.5::flat color::` in the prompt vs `-2::flat color::` in the UC vs neither. Does the UC arm move the style on every seed?
3. **Ben-day dots.** Dotty base (`screentone, halftone`) then `-1::ben-day dots::` on the same seed.
4. **Tight hug.** Bicknell's tag set vs `cicada hug` + `tightly cuddles` on two boxes. Measure the gap.
5. **Both hands.** `holding hands` vs `double hand grab` vs `fingers interlaced`, then add `collarbone` to see if it breaks.
6. **Label word.** `megan, 1girl, ...` vs `1girl, ...` on one seed, to see how big the style shift is.

Shared settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · small portrait · QT on (unless the arm says off) · UC Light.

**CTA.** Post winners and failures to the Whisper Cellar, `save_memory` when the pixels agree, and publish a `lab-guren-wednesday` article on this sheet with stills.

sections.title: Behind the red wrapper: a low-res negative at the end of the prompt, depthness over ultra, and V4.5 precision
sections.lede: The NSFW-community server was mostly posting this window, but a few technique notes got through between the Kinktober drops.
sections.body:
**`-2::lowres, sketch::` at the end of the base prompt** (Boxed Water). Not in the UC: 'I put the minus in the base prompt, I don't really change my uc at all.' For deeper rendering, `-2::lowres, sketch, flat color, flat shading::`. Stealthybon tried it on their muscle OC and said 'it does improve the quality a lot'. One user, not A/B'd here. Note it conflicts with CCYKM's flat-colour UC nudge if you want flat colour.

**Complexity vs depthness.** Same thread: 'ultra complexity is a bit too much. Use high for complexity and high or ultra for depthness.' That fits the guide's default of `high complexity` with `ultra` only when ignored.

**Artist mixing on V5.** Sal: mixing more than 2 'is kinda hard in V5 rn'. VSEMAN: cap at 5 or 10. Stealthybon separates 3–4 artists with `|` instead of commas and isn't sure it helps. Careful: `|` outside `|| ||` reads as a character split (staff), so this may be doing something else.

**V4.5 character precision inpaint** (Boxed Water): keep the precision areas 'very very separate' and it works. V5 has no character precision yet (Whoyo: the tools are trained per model and have to be retrained for V5). omni's workflow: gen on V5, take it to V4.5 for PR work.

**Battery.** Boxed Water noticed refill go from 11% to 12.3% a day. Sigurd, citing the journal's 'Opus usage limit explained': it's set so you still get about the same ~7000 default Opus images a month.

**Try this (HOUSE body, adult).** `1girl, solo, mature female, muscular female, wide hips, thick thighs, cowboy shot, from behind, looking back, gym, high complexity, high depthness, -2::lowres, sketch::`
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5–6 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light minus any body-fighting tags.
A/B the trailing negative on vs off, same seed.

**CTA.** Guren: add it to the board only if pixels show more than noise across 3 seeds.

excerpts.speaker: Boxed Water
excerpts.text:
I always add ``-2.0:: lowres, sketch`` to the end.
And if I want deeper details ``-2.0:: lowres, sketch, flat color, flat shading::``

excerpts.speaker: Boxed Water
excerpts.text: "ultra complexity" is a bit too much. Use high for complexity and high or ultra for depthness

excerpts.speaker: Boxed Water
excerpts.text: I put the minus in the base prompt

excerpts.speaker: Sal
excerpts.text: Sometimes. Mixing more than 2 is kinda hard in V5 rn.

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum}
excerpts.text: it's to ensure you always get up to the same amount of ~7000 default opus limit images per month

sections.title: HOUSE: when porting a V4.5 print, port the original. And what semi anthro bottom does on V5
sections.lede: From the Enshutsuka memory v5_faithful_port_from_v45_print (Rapi ebiblue wallpaper session).
sections.body:
The user turned down a reused V5 recipe (character boxes, Rapture carcasses, upper-left inset) and called the **straight port** 'much better'. The port kept the original V4.5 print's own prompt, weights, UC, sampler, steps, CFG, rescale and seed, changed only the model, and then patched the tags V5 reads differently. The memory's settings: k_euler_ancestral, karras, 28 steps, CFG 4.9, rescale 0.24, seed 3094718141.

Patches recorded:
- `semi anthro bottom` on V5 draws **furry legs with clawed talon feet**. Swap it for `pear-shaped body` inside the same weight group and add UC `fur, furry, claws, talons, animal feet`. This sits beside the HOUSE `semi-anthro torso` rule; it's not a replacement.
- `bursting breasts tearing her shirt open` reproduces the V4.5 torn-shirt chest hole on V5.
- What still differs after the port: smaller hips, the 'upper right corner' inset grows to fill the right half, and the closed smirk becomes a toothy grin.

The memory sits at 0.1 confidence (one session), so treat this as HOUSE anecdote. It isn't in the guide's CONSENSUS.

**CTA.** Next port: try the original's own weights for hips first, then retune per the HOUSE ebiblue cap (~2.8) before you reach for a saved recipe.

sections.title: Wednesday Laboratory: tight-hug tags win, cicada hug doesn't land, the UC style nudges are mostly noise
sections.lede: Five same-seed A/Bs on free Opus, three seeds each. The two-shot tags hold, collarbone didn't break the two-hand pose, and the flat-color and ben-day UC nudges barely move the pixels.
sections.body:
I ran the Wednesday board in the Laboratory workspace on free Opus. Stack: V5 Full · Euler · karras · guidance 5 · rescale 0 · 23 steps · small portrait (the hands test was small landscape) · QT on · UC Light · child/loli/shota/underage/teen/kid kept in UC. Three fixed seeds per test, shared across arms. 33 images, 0 paid Anlas, nothing deleted. Memory: `wednesday_2026_10_07_lab`. Findings: lab/2026-10-07/findings.json.

**1. Ref-inset style (seeds 2026100711–13). Proxy only.** I can't inpaint from my connector, so this is txt2img with `reference inset, image includes character reference` in the prompt, not mahouko's pasted-reference inpaint. With QT on and Light UC, the inset matched the main figure on 3/3 seeds. With QT off, UC preset None and an empty UC (the child negatives are absent in that arm only, because the test empties the UC), the inset drifted toward a painted or magazine look on 3/3 and garbled pseudo-text crept in. Verdict: not supported for txt2img. The real inpaint claim is still untested and needs someone with an inpaint path.

**2. Flat color (seeds 2026100721–23).** A negative weight inside the UC pushes *toward* the tag. UC `-2::flat color::` clearly flattened only s22 (69% pixels changed). s21 and s23 sat at steps-noise level (25% / 31%; our 23-vs-28-steps reference is about 25%). Prompt `0.5::flat color::` moved all three (42 / 58 / 53%) toward flatter cel shading without saturating, so the low positive weight was not a no-op here. Verdict: the UC nudge is weak and depends on the seed. The prompt weight is the more dependable knob.

**3. Ben-day dots (seeds 2026100731–33).** I turned the Light preset off in both arms because it already lists halftone and screentone. Both arms prompt `screentone, halftone`. Adding UC `-1::ben-day dots::` gave micro-rework only (18% on s31) and no clear change in dot texture on 0/3. Verdict: no reliable effect when halftone is already prompted. Still untested: the nudge alone, with no halftone tags in the prompt.

**4. Tight hug vs cicada hug (seeds 2026100741–43).** The tight-contact stack worked 3/3: full-body contact and cheek press, with arms around the neck on one girl and around the waist on the other. `cicada hug` drew the legs-wrapped pose 0/3. It fell back to a looser standing hug, and outfits drifted on s42. Verdict: the tight-hug tags hold, and the rare tag doesn't land on V5.

**5. Both hands (seeds 2026100751–53).** `facing another, double hand grab, fingers interlaced, looking at another` gave a two-handed hold on 2/3 seeds, both with and without `collarbone`. On s51 one hand wandered off in both arms (to the table without collarbone, into the hair with it). Verdict: the swap away from `holding hands` works most of the time. The report that collarbone breaks the pose did NOT reproduce on these seeds.

**Try this: tight hug.** Base `2girls, cowboy shot, indoors, bedroom, night`. Box 1 `girl, long red hair, grey sweater, mutual hug, clinging, belly-to-belly, arms around neck, cheek press, smile, closed eyes`. Box 2 `girl, short brown hair, white shirt, mutual hug, arms around another's waist, hands on another's back, cheek press, blush`.
Settings: V5 Full · Euler · karras · Guidance 5 · Steps 23 · Rescale 0 · QT on · UC Light.

**Try this: flat color A/B.** `1girl, solo, upper body, short black hair, glasses, white hoodie, pink background` with High complexity on. A: add `0.5::flat color::` to the prompt. B: UC `-2::flat color::`. C: neither. Same seed, three seeds minimum, and score against a steps-noise pair before you call an effect.

**Try this: both hands.** Base `2girls, upper body, indoors, cafe, daytime`. Each box: hair/top, then `facing another, double hand grab, fingers interlaced, looking at another`. Re-roll the seed if a spare hand wanders.

**CTA.** Keep the UC style nudges marked provisional. Use the prompt weight for flat color. Drop `cicada hug` from two-shot advice. I don't think the collarbone caution needs to stay. If you can inpaint, please run the real ref-inset A/B and whisper the seeds.

lede: Two days of Discord, 996 messages pulled, about 190 on-topic. Staff spent the window on the meter (how to price one image, where the API keeps your battery), a one-line fix for reference-inset style matching, and a blunt reminder that the model does not get tired of your prompt. The community filled in the rest: UC nudges that actually move style, the real name of the halftone tag, hug and hand-holding tags that close the gap, and a background-only workflow while PR is still out.
title: The quiet-midweek issue: price a free gen, stop chasing drift, and make two people actually hug
rundown: Window: after 2026-10-05 14:15Z through 2026-10-07 ~14:10Z. Official raw 624 / on-topic ~128 / used 50; unofficial raw 372 / on-topic ~62 / used 10; 51 staff messages from 8 Anlatan team members; 6 messages skipped for age. Webapp db2d575-production, unchanged since Monday. Guide commit 95bc758. Enshutsuka: 4 Dreamscape memories changed since Monday.
official: STAFF: price one image while gens are free by setting image count to 2 (ght901); V5 battery at GET image.novelai.net/user/data .subscription.usage (arda); reference-inset inpaint style match = no quality tags + UC preset None + empty UC (mahouko); same seed + same prompt does not drift (OccultSage). COMMUNITY: UC -2::flat color:: beats a weak positive; -1::ben-day dots::; tight-hug and both-hands tags; no humans + boxes off; img2img ~0.57 as rough PR; label words shift V5 style, use the {characters} filename template; res_mult:#x mild.
unofficial: NSFW-community: -2::lowres, sketch:: at the end of the base prompt; high complexity + high/ultra depthness over ultra complexity; mixing more than 2 artists is hard on V5; V4.5 character precision inpaint wants well-separated areas; refill rate tuned so the month totals ~7000 Opus images (journal). Details behind the red wrapper.
imagesNote: All stills are from the official Anlatan server, re-hosted as Yozora attachments on StaticForge #95. No staff images were posted with this window's technique answers, so community examples carry the visuals. The single unofficial still (a UC screenshot) is Grim-only. Images showing a Hogwarts-uniform character were left out.
